prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange my preferred configuration is unchanged: a single prize part on B008 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. All six of us reached it independently, and the round-1 files show that the agreement rests on the same scientific chain and not on the opening count. Holst established GLP-1 secretion and insulinotropic action in humans, Mojsov identified the biologically active truncated peptide GLP-1(7-36), and Drucker defined proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor actions. The result is a drug class with replicated glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal benefit in large independent outcome trials, so there is no maturity question. The citation I propose is deliberately worded to name the physiology and the active form and to state that these made the therapies possible. That records the translation without crediting the drug engineering itself, and it keeps a basic discoverer in the third slot.
statement.case_against: The weakness is attribution and I have not found a way round it. Four credited names do not fit three slots, and Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener and colleagues, who are not on the credited list, cannot be settled from the supplied material. Knudsen's long-acting analogues are what patients receive, so a basic-discovery trio can be read as stopping short of the step that changed practice. I weigh that as a real cost but not a decisive one, because the cost of dropping a discoverer to correct it is of the same kind. I also see no clean second part: B017 and B001 each have an unresolved credit gap or a narrower scope, and adding either would force a cut to the B008 trio under the three-person limit.

responses.point: Marie keeps Knudsen in the third slot with a citation covering both GLP-1 physiology and the development of incretin-based therapies, and says she would accept Mojsov if the committee narrows the achievement to discovery biology.
responses.response: Your reply to the chair's question helps, and I agree the narrowing should be stated openly, so I state it: the achievement I propose is the physiology and the active form, with the therapies named in the citation as the consequence. I do not think that leaves out the drugs, because the citation says what the discoveries made possible. My remaining difference with you is about what the third slot rewards. The analogue work is superb development, but the principle it exploited, that the truncated peptide is the active hormone, comes from the discovery side, and I would not remove a discoverer to make room for a developer when the citation can carry the translation. I would move toward your configuration only if the committee finds Mojsov's claim to the active peptide weaker than I currently judge it.

responses.point: As chair, Per says he prefers Mojsov but would not block a Knudsen substitution if Mojsov's priority is judged too disputed, and asks the committee to settle the third name before turning to a second part.
responses.response: I agree with the order you set: the third name and citation first, a second part only afterwards. On the evidence, I read Mojsov's priority as contested, which is different from unsupported, and the supplied material gives no basis for treating the dispute as grounds for exclusion. Habener's absence from the credited list is a real gap, but it is a gap in the candidate file and not a reason to give her slot to a different kind of contribution. I would revisit if the committee holds evidence that Habener's group, and not Mojsov, identified the active form. On that evidence I would then ask whether the slot should go to him and not to Knudsen, since both questions are about the active peptide.

responses.point: Thomas holds B017 and B001 as alternatives and not as a second part, because he sees no clean way to add a part without cutting B008's core trio, and prefers June and Sadelain over a trio with Rosenberg.
responses.response: I agree with your count and I have tested it. A two-part configuration is possible only if B008 shrinks to two names, and neither Holst plus Drucker alone nor any pairing with Mojsov is a better-supported prize than the trio. Splitting the three-person limit would weaken a case that is strong because the chain is intact. On B001 I keep my round-1 view that it is a credible later prize, since nusinersen has about ten years of use and a single-disease, single-platform scope. On B017 I now agree with you and with Marie that the Eshhar question should be answered before any CAR-T allocation, and that June and Sadelain is the more defensible pair if it is taken up.

responses.point: Rickard rests the case on established glycaemic, weight, cardiovascular and renal outcomes, would keep neurological benefit out of it, and would let Knudsen replace Drucker or Mojsov only if the priority evidence for the active peptide proves weaker than he believes.
responses.response: I agree on both points and keep the citation free of any neurological claim. I would add that the condition you give for a substitution is the right test, and that it should apply to Mojsov and not to Drucker. Drucker's work on proglucagon-derived peptide biology and receptor actions is the part of the chain that connects the physiology to the drug target, and I see no scientific argument for removing him. I should also correct a detail in my round-1 reply to you: I included Rosenberg in an earlier ballot position, but I now hold that adoptive transfer is a separate line from CAR design, so my B017 preference is June and Sadelain and not a trio.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov or an early contributor not on the credited list, such as Habener, has the stronger claim to identification of the active GLP-1 peptide; I cannot resolve this from the supplied material and it is the main point on which my configuration could change.
Whether the committee will accept a citation that states the therapeutic consequence without crediting analogue development, or will require Knudsen in the configuration.
Whether the Eshhar gap rules out B017 as a future prize and whether B001 can be assigned cleanly, since Singh, Melki and Lefebvre are outside the credited names.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for B008, B017, B001 or any other shortlisted candidate. I disclose co-authorship with Rickard Sandberg and others, and my authorship of the 2016 spatial transcriptomics paper. None of these involves a credited name on the shortlist, and shared institutional affiliation is not treated as a tie. No change since round 1; I do not recuse.
